evidence: "# DFS to count critical nodes in subtree"; "m = n-1"; "if t <= 1: print(0)"
affordance_in_statement: The pool of axioms is minimally complete: there are exactly m = n − 1 available axioms, and if you were to adopt all of them, the entire system would admit exactly two valid truth assignments
removal_suggestion: There is no semantics-preserving wording change that removes this reduction: pairwise equivalence axioms together with the stated two-assignment guarantee intrinsically form a connected tree. To defeat the shortcut, the scenario would have to stop guaranteeing that the axiom graph is connected and acyclic, for example by allowing arbitrary redundant or disconnected axiom pools while retaining the same input syntax.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses the connected n-vertex, n−1-edge axiom graph as a tree and computes the minimum subtree containing the critical propositions.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: there are exactly m = n − 1 available axioms, and ... all of them ... admit exactly two valid truth assignments

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Treats synchronization as connectivity in the tree and handles the t=1 case as an empty selected subtree.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: the t critical propositions must all hold the exact same truth value as each other

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Builds an undirected weighted adjacency graph and applies the standard tree connectivity/subtree solution.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: Each axiom establishes a logical equivalence between two propositions u and v

common_affordance: The equivalence constraints turn the axiom pool into a connected tree, so the critical propositions are synchronized exactly when they lie in one connected selected subtree.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Its UnionFind-based approach uses greedy component unions rather than correctly selecting the minimum-cost subtree containing all critical vertices, so it can mishandle Steiner vertices and weighted paths.

recommended_edit: Because this is a structural property of the task rather than incidental wording, no rephrasing can defeat all survivors while preserving the task. The only effective edit is to remove the minimal-completeness guarantee and state that the m=n−1 pairwise axioms may form an arbitrary disconnected or cyclic graph; this preserves the input/output formats and examples but eliminates the tree reduction.
